name: Film Noir
description: In a rainy detective office the color drains away into hard black and white shadows.

wardrobe.man: a 1940s grey suit, a white shirt, a dark tie and a fedora
wardrobe.woman: a 1940s fitted dark dress and a wide-brimmed hat
wardrobe.person: a 1940s grey suit and a fedora

scene_prompt: Create a new cinematic film still in {aspect_words} format. {references} The {subject} is the only person in the new still, with exactly {their} face, eyes, nose, jaw, hairline, hairstyle, hair colour{facial_hair}, skin tone and build{identity_notes}. The clothing, the place and the light come only from this description. The {subject} stands by the window of a 1940s detective office at night, turned three-quarters toward the camera, wearing {wardrobe}. Rain runs down the glass, the light of a streetlamp comes through half-open venetian blinds, a desk lamp glows green on a wooden desk with a typewriter and a rotary telephone. Medium shot at eye level, the {subject} on the right third, the window on the left. Cinematic photography in full color, warm tungsten desk light and cool blue rain light from the window. Correct human anatomy, natural skin texture, sharp focus on the {subject}, a plain frosted glass door and blank papers throughout.
effect_prompt: Use the provided start image as the first frame. The {subject} ALREADY stands by the rainy window, eyes on a point just past the camera, and stays there for the whole shot. Within the first second the color drains out of the whole image, and from then to the last frame the shot is pure high-contrast black and white film noir: the green lamp turns a pale grey glow, the warm light turns silver, the light through the venetian blinds sharpens into hard white stripes across {their} face and the wall, the shadows deepen to ink black, and a soft film grain settles over everything. The {subject} slowly turns {their} head toward the window. GRAYSCALE LAW: from 1.0 s to the last frame every pixel is a shade of grey; any visible color = failed take. The camera pushes in slowly. Sound: steady rain on glass, a distant lonely saxophone note, the creak of an old building. Photorealistic, cinematic visual effects, classic black and white film noir with hard shadows and film grain, sharp detail, stable picture.
generic_prompt: Use the provided start image as the first frame. The color drains out of the scene from the edges inward, until the whole shot is high-contrast black and white film noir: hard white light and ink-black shadows across the {subject}, and a soft film grain settling over everything. The camera keeps the same framing and the same movement it already has. Sound: steady rain, a distant lonely saxophone note. Photorealistic, cinematic visual effects, classic black and white film noir with hard shadows and film grain, sharp detail, stable picture.
